lift.name: Lifted Tile
lift.tagline: One widget tile lifted off the board, tilted mid-placement: the app's core gesture as a mark that still reads at 16 px in the tray.
lift.concept: The board is the teacher's canvas and the tile is a widget mid-placement: the familiar tile board is fused into one calm sage slab with a single recessed socket in its top-right cell, and the terracotta tile that belongs there is lifted, tilted 14 degrees and floating over the corner under a soft warm grey-green shadow, the app's core verb frozen at the moment of lifting a widget onto the classroom. Nothing in the silhouette is a dot grid: it is one heavy rounded slab, one bite and one askew chip, which is why the tray glyph is recognisably this app where the current 3x3 grid is not. Colour stays inside the family: the same warm off-white to pale-sage plate, the board in the mid sages (#97c2ad to #76a896 around #86b49f), the socket in the deep sages #4c8571 to #65a28d so it reads as a recess under one top-left light, the tile in the terracottas (#ee9f84, #d4775c, #c25e42) as the single warm accent, and every shadow in warm grey-green #364a42 rather than black. The glyph is the same three shapes in one ink at the same positions, with the socket opening into a 92-unit knockout around the tile so the tile reads as floating in front of the board; every feature and gap is at or above the 64-unit minimum (knockout 92, rim 108, socket-to-gap channel 98) and the body was morphologically opened by 32 units so no hairline of ink survives at 18 px. Every element sits inside the squircle plate (the tile's corner clears the plate's corner arc by 42 units) so the Windows/Linux full-bleed derivation loses nothing, and for macOS Icon Composer it splits cleanly into the existing three layers: background plate, board with socket, lifted tile.
lift.glyphNotes: At 18 px it is a solid rounded block with a square bite out of its upper right and a smaller tilted square floating off that corner behind a light gap: a tile lifting off a board, not a grid, a copy icon or an external-link arrow. At 16 px white-on-dark the gap still resolves to a clean diagonal hairline of background, so the two shapes never fuse into one blob.

lift2.name: Lifted Tile
lift2.tagline: One tile lifting off a board of running widgets — the app's core gesture, drawn so it survives the tray.
lift2.concept: A cream 2×2 board sits on a deep-sage plate with its true top-right cell cut out, and that same tile is lifting away on a 14° tilt, overhanging the board's top and right edges so the outer silhouette is "a square minus a corner cell, with the cell escaping" rather than a box with a badge. The socket is the tile's exact 240-unit footprint with the same R60 corner (its filleted inner corner is the tell), and two faint dusty-rose seams complete the 2×2 so the read is "several widgets, one being placed". Colour does figure/ground by luminance, not hue: cream board (L≈0.87) over deep sage (≈0.10) with the terracotta chip (≈0.28) sitting between them, so nothing depends on the isoluminant sage/terracotta pair, and the saturated plate holds full-bleed on light Windows Start and GNOME grids where the old off-white plate dissolved. One top-left light throughout: a single diagonal gradient per surface, a soft warm-green drop under the board and a larger, more offset one under the chip so the chip reads higher. The glyph is the same three parts — L-board, corner socket, tilted chip — with the socket widened by a 104-unit knockout so the chip separates cleanly at 16 px; put the 64 px icon beside the 18 pt menu-bar glyph and they are obviously one mark.
lift2.glyphNotes: At 16–18 px it reads as a chunky L-shaped board with one square tile tilting out of its missing top-right cell: two closed masses (arms 296 units, chip 400, narrowest gap 147, chip overhanging the board's top and right edges by ~100), so the outline is asymmetric and cannot be mistaken for a plain box, a dot, an app grid, a copy icon or a notification badge.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1024 1024" width="1024" height="1024">
  <!-- Lifted Tile: a 2x2 board with its true top-right cell cut out, and that cell's tile lifting away on a 14 degree tilt. -->
  <!-- Board: 800 square at (64,162), R100. Notch = tile footprint (400) + 104 knockout on its two inner sides; inner fillet 140. Arms 296 wide. -->
  <path id="lift2g-board" fill="#000" d="M164 162 L360 162 L360 526 A140 140 0 0 0 500 666 L864 666 L864 862 A100 100 0 0 1 764 962 L164 962 A100 100 0 0 1 64 862 L64 262 A100 100 0 0 1 164 162 Z"/>
  <!-- Chip: the same 400 tile, r64, centre displaced (+72,-72) from the socket centre (664,362), tilted 14 degrees; overhangs the board's top and right edges by ~100. Narrowest gap to the board: 147. -->
  <rect id="lift2g-chip" fill="#000" x="536" y="90" width="400" height="400" rx="64" transform="rotate(-14 736 290)"/>
</svg>
